title: Intervention Efforts Failing to Turn Tide for Yen - 3-Minutes MLIV
titleChinese: 干预努力未能扭转日元走势 - 3分钟MLIV
summary: 日本和美国的干预努力未能扭转日元走势，尽管有多轮确认的干预和美财长的警告，日元仍然表现不佳，日本官员希望日元能跌破155，但未能实现，市场人士认为日本央行的沟通努力不够，美联储加息预期和地缘政治因素也是影响因素，油价和中东局势的不确定性也使得干预努力变得困难

transcript.english: Adam, are we still thinking about the yen this morning?
transcript.chinese: Adam，我们今天早上还在关注日元吗？

transcript.english: I mean, somebody sent this was yesterday's real refocus, wasn't it?
transcript.chinese: 我是说，有人认为昨天是真正的重新关注点，对吧？

transcript.english: But today we see at the end, um, underperforming a little bit.
transcript.chinese: 但是今天我们看到，嗯，稍微表现不佳了一点。

transcript.english: And that's perhaps not what those who want a drink again wanted to say.
transcript.chinese: 也许这并不是那些想再喝一杯的人想要说的。

transcript.english: So what's what's our latest conclusion as to whether this intervention by the Japanese and the Americans will work?
transcript.chinese: 那么，我们最新的结论是什么，关于日本和美国的干预是否会有效？

transcript.english: Yeah.
transcript.chinese: 是的。

transcript.english: I think when you consider the fact that we've had a couple of confirmed rounds of intervention now, which also coordinated with the US, have had warnings from U.S.
transcript.chinese: 我认为，当你考虑到我们已经进行了几轮确认的干预，而且这些干预也与美国进行了协调，并且收到了美国的警告时，

transcript.english: Treasury Secretary, it's been particularly disappointing.
transcript.chinese: 美国财政部长，这一点尤其令人失望。

transcript.english: I mean, even at the trough, we didn't really break through the lows.
transcript.chinese: 我的意思是，即使在谷底，我们也没有真正突破低点。

transcript.english: I think Japanese officials would have been hoping they would have got below 155.
transcript.chinese: 我认为日本官员原本希望能将日元汇率降低到155以下。

transcript.english: So I think when you also consider the positioning backdrop mean yen short stay the highest since July 2024, dollar positioning was at record highs in some measures.
transcript.chinese: 因此，我认为当你也考虑到仓位背景时，日元空头仓位自2024年7月以来最高，美元仓位在某些衡量指标中创下了历史新高。

transcript.english: It's a pretty pitiful response.
transcript.chinese: 这是一个相当可怜的反应。

transcript.english: And what we've seen and I think, you know, ultimately there's a couple of things at play here.
transcript.chinese: 而且我们已经看到，我认为，你知道，归根结底这里有几件事情在起作用。

transcript.english: One is that the BMJ just isn't playing its role.
transcript.chinese: 一个是日本央行（BMJ）没有发挥其作用。

transcript.english: We kind of get this continued communication effort from them that they may do something at some point in the future.
transcript.chinese: 我们从他们那里得到了持续的沟通努力，表明他们可能在未来某个时候采取行动。

transcript.english: In a world this price of fed hikes, that just isn't good enough.
transcript.chinese: 在这种美联储加息的环境下，这还不够。

transcript.english: And we saw some angst about the BOJ overnight.
transcript.chinese: 我们看到市场对日本央行（BOJ）overnight表现出了一些担忧。

transcript.english: So that sort of ten year JGB auction as well.
transcript.chinese: 因此，十年期日本国债（JGB）拍卖也是如此。

transcript.english: So that's also a friend of mine but also as well.
transcript.chinese: 所以，这也是我的一个朋友，但同时也是如此。

transcript.english: Quite simply, from a geopolitical standpoint, with something out of control for Japanese officials is that they need this war ends.
transcript.chinese: 简单来说，从地缘政治角度来看，对于日本官员来说，有一件事失控了，那就是他们需要这场战争结束。

transcript.english: They need oil prices to come lower.
transcript.chinese: 他们需要油价下降。

transcript.english: Yeah.
transcript.chinese: 是的。

transcript.english: So it's actually it's kind of a waste of money on this intervention unless you get a step in from the be.
transcript.chinese: 所以，除非你能从后端获得一个台阶，否则在这种干预措施上花钱实际上是一种浪费。

transcript.english: Okay.
transcript.chinese: 好。

transcript.english: Just on that geopolitical point.
transcript.chinese: 就那一点地缘政治。

transcript.english: You know, the headlines flying around, the comments flying around, Donald Trump being pretty, uh, angry towards around them, saying that the talks aren't even happening.
transcript.chinese: 你知道，到处都是头条新闻和评论，唐纳德·特朗普对他们的态度相当，呃，愤怒，称谈判甚至都没有发生。

transcript.english: What does the market need to to have greater progress?
transcript.chinese: 市场需要什么才能取得更大的进展？

transcript.english: Yeah.
transcript.chinese: 是的。

transcript.english: I mean, I think there's a pretty high bar at the moment for success.
transcript.chinese: 我是说，我认为目前成功的门槛相当高。

transcript.english: You know, we saw Trump be relatively bullish on the prospects over the weekend, the same time Iran was talking with a man by the Straits of Hormuz, voicing that the full reopening of it and traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is still particularly low than in other parts of Middle East.
transcript.chinese: 你知道，周末我们看到特朗普对前景相对乐观，与此同时伊朗在霍尔木兹海峡与一名男子交谈，表示完全重新开放霍尔木兹海峡以及通过霍尔木兹海峡的交通流量仍然比中东其他地区低。

transcript.english: Traffic flows are relatively low.
transcript.chinese: 交通流量相对较低。

transcript.english: I think, you know, obviously we need to see Trump's bullishness over the weekend reciprocated from Iran, but we just simply not seeing that.
transcript.chinese: 我认为，显然，我们需要看到伊朗在周末对特朗普的乐观态度做出回应，但我们就是没有看到这一点。

transcript.english: The moment that you're saying that the U.S. needs to change its behavior, I think it even if we do get an interim peace agreement, then I think the markets can be particularly wary of it, given that we've already had one broken down and then since the onset of conflict, as far as I can tell, there's been no progress on nuclear.
transcript.chinese: 当你说美国需要改变其行为时，我认为即使我们达成临时和平协议，市场也会特别警惕，因为我们已经经历了一次破裂，而且自冲突开始以来，据我所知，核问题上没有任何进展。

transcript.english: So I think, you know, energy prices will stay sticky.
transcript.chinese: 所以，我认为能源价格会保持坚挺。

transcript.english: And in that environment, upside for bonds is limited.
transcript.chinese: 在这种环境下，债券的上涨空间是有限的。

transcript.english: You know, particularly in the US where there's a real rate story then also for Europe.
transcript.chinese: 你知道的，特别是在美国，有一个实际利率的故事，也适用于欧洲。

transcript.english: Yeah.
transcript.chinese: 是的。

transcript.english: Let me ask you about the data point of the week, which is known from payrolls to you on Friday.
transcript.chinese: 让我问你关于本周的数据点，从周五的非农就业报告来看。

transcript.english: Of course, as in and are we concerned.
transcript.chinese: 当然，我们关心。

transcript.english: Last week we saw that steepening trade partly due to the fed narrative rather than the data, but we don't really know how the fed is going to react to data.
transcript.chinese: 上周，我们看到收益率曲线陡峭化的交易，部分是由于美联储的说法，而不是数据，但我们真的不知道美联储将如何对数据做出反应。

transcript.english: That's by design and what has told us.
transcript.chinese: 这是故意为之，并且已经告诉我们了。

transcript.english: So how are you thinking the market could respond then to this said nonfarm payrolls?
transcript.chinese: 那么，你认为市场将如何对这份非农就业报告做出反应呢？

transcript.english: Yeah, I mean it's a big data point.
transcript.chinese: 是的，我是说这是一个重要的数据点。

transcript.english: You know, we need to play the ball, not the referee's, Kevin Warsh says.
transcript.chinese: 你知道，我们需要关注数据本身，而不是评判决策者，凯文·沃什说。

transcript.english: And any data point now is much higher volume than other would have otherwise would have been.
transcript.chinese: 现在任何数据点的关注度都远高于其他情况下原本会有的水平。

transcript.english: There's plenty of scope to reprise a September hike only price around 65%.
transcript.chinese: 有足够的空间重新计入9月加息预期，目前价格仅在65%左右。

transcript.english: I think it's more interesting if we get a hot report.
transcript.chinese: 我认为如果我们得到一个强于预期的数据就更有趣了。

transcript.english: The markets really ramp up these wages at the front end.
transcript.chinese: 市场真正推高了收益率曲线短端的工资。

transcript.english: I think the fed is getting behind the curve, but also the back end of the curve.
transcript.chinese: 我认为美联储正在落后于形势，不仅如此，也包括收益率曲线长端。

transcript.english: There's a real rate story which is really driving things as well.
transcript.chinese: 实际利率的故事也在推动着市场。

transcript.english: We saw strong I said yesterday.
transcript.chinese: 我们昨天看到强劲的表现。

transcript.english: And if you see a strong NFP do we start getting that yields towards 5.3%.
transcript.chinese: 如果你看到强劲的非农就业报告，我们是否开始将收益率推向5.3%。

transcript.english: And that also become a cross asset story as well.
transcript.chinese: 这也成为一个影响多类资产的交易主线。
